title: God speaks as to friends (Dei Verbum 2)
hook: God speaks to people as friends and lives among them
tomorrow: why does the priest kiss the book at Mass?

segments.voice: Yesterday, how to read a Church document: its kind, its Latin name, its numbered paragraphs. The line was numbered paragraphs.

The voice memo, the long careful text, the two-word reply: friends talk more than one way. When the bishops of the Second Vatican Council set out to explain how God makes himself known, they could have reached for a courtroom, a classroom or a rulebook. In paragraph two of Dei Verbum they reached for friendship. The invisible God, they write, speaks to people as friends. Which leaves a question people still argue about at the kitchen table: if God talks like a friend, how should anyone talk back?
screen: `FRIENDS TALK MORE THAN ONE WAY.` → `NOT A RULEBOOK: A FRIEND.` → `HOW DO YOU TALK BACK?`

segments.voice: First, the paragraph. Dei Verbum 2 says God speaks out of the abundance of his love, to invite people into fellowship with himself. The picture isn't new. Exodus says the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, the way someone speaks to a friend, and in John's Gospel Jesus says, "But I have called you friends." God speaks through deeds and words bound together, the council adds, and Christ is the fullness of it: God speaks as to friends, and lives among them. Second, one answer: plainly. Friends don't read each other scripts. Say what happened today, in your own words, and leave room to listen. Teresa of Avila, earlier on this path, described prayer as a friendly conversation with the one who loves us. Third, the other answer: in shared words. Old friends have sayings worn smooth with use. When the disciples asked Jesus how to pray, he gave them words, the Our Father. The rosary, the psalms and the prayers of the Mass are words the Church keeps saying together, and on the day your own words run out, they're still there. Fourth, where that leaves a person. The council's paragraph doesn't pick between them. Some people pray both ways before breakfast.
screen: `OUT OF LOVE, AN INVITATION.` · `PLAIN WORDS, LIKE A FRIEND.` · `SHARED WORDS, LIKE OLD FRIENDS.` · `THE PARAGRAPH DOESN'T PICK.` · then, large: `AS FRIENDS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and sit the way you'd sit across from a good friend, unhurried. If you pray, say one real thing about today to God in plain words, then leave the rest of the quiet for listening. If you don't, simply notice what it's like to be spoken to as a friend, not a stranger.
God speaks as to friends. Dei Verbum's picture of revelation: an invitation into friendship, in deeds and words, made full in Christ. Today's word.
screen: `GOD SPEAKS AS TO FRIENDS — today's word`.

segments.voice: One line to keep: as friends, which is how the council says God speaks, and lives among people. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics pray both in their own words and with set prayers such as the Our Father and the rosary; Dei Verbum 2 is often read in classes on revelation and in preparing adults for baptism.

fork.setup: your friend says memorized prayers are fake, like reading a script to someone you love. what's the strongest case for the other side?
options: old friends share words, and Jesus himself gave the Our Father.
memorized prayers are faster, so they fit a busy day better.
God only listens to official words the Church has approved.
fork.reveal: when the disciples asked how to pray, Jesus gave them words. shared words can be friendship too, especially when your own run out.

original.note: Latin in Dei Verbum 2: God addresses people as friends.

what it means: God, out of love, speaks to people as friends, in deeds and words, and lives among them, fully in Christ.
what a scholar hears: Dei Verbum 2 drawing on Exodus 33:11 and John 15:14–15, with deeds and words bound together and Christ as mediator and fullness of revelation.

chat.says: abuela says pray for the speech with a rosary. dad says just talk to God. who's right??
options: Both have a case: friends talk plainly, and old friends share words. Try both.
Dad. If God speaks as a friend, set prayers are just reading off a script.
Abuela. Talking to God casually is rude; only the old words really count.
chat.meaning: Dei Verbum 2 pictures God speaking to people as friends; plain words and the Church's shared prayers are both ways friends talk back.

Dei Verbum.meaning: Vatican II's constitution on God's word; Latin for the word of God

Moses.meaning: the leader to whom, Exodus says, the Lord spoke face to face

Exodus.meaning: the second book of the Bible, the story of leaving Egypt

Our Father.meaning: the prayer Jesus taught his disciples

rosary.meaning: a prayer of repeated Hail Marys, counted on beads

notes: Dei Verbum 2 is paraphrased (the official English is not public domain): confirm 'out of the abundance of his love', 'speaks to men as friends and lives among them', 'invite and take them into fellowship', 'deeds and words having an inner unity', and Christ as 'mediator and fullness of all revelation'.
Exodus 33:11 is paraphrased; John 15:15 quoted from Douay-Rheims: confirm the exact wording.
Teresa, Life 8: prayer as friendly intercourse/conversation with the one we know loves us; paraphrased (modern translations are not public domain). Confirm.
Debate shape: the two views (plain conversational prayer; set, shared prayers) are both within Catholic practice and both voiced; the paragraph is not claimed to settle it.
Original game: 'tamquam amicos' is from the Latin of DV 2 (alloquitur tamquam amicos); confirm with a Latinist.
